course: Pizza Oven Construction - Wood Fired 12 Pizza

lessons.title: Applying Stucco or Stone Veneer
lessons.body:
Stucco is the most common finish for wood-fired ovens in Africa because it is cheap, easy to apply, and handles heat well. You will need Portland cement, sharp sand, and water. Mix 1 part cement to 3 parts sand for the scratch coat, and 1 part cement to 4 parts sand for the finish coat. Add water until the mix is like thick peanut butter. For a 12-pizza oven, you will need about 4 bags of cement and 12 wheelbarrows of sand for two coats.

Before stucco, dampen the oven's concrete or brick surface with water so it doesn't suck moisture from the mix. Apply the scratch coat about 1 cm thick using a steel trowel. Scratch the surface with a nail or rake to create grooves for the next coat. Let it cure for 24 hours, then spray with water twice a day for 3 days. The brown coat goes on 1 cm thick, then the finish coat 5 mm thick. Use a wooden float to create a rough texture or a sponge for a smooth finish.

If using stone veneer, you need flat stones, mortar mix, and a grinder with a diamond blade. Start from the bottom and work up. Apply a 1 cm layer of mortar to the back of each stone and press it onto the oven. Keep a 1 cm gap between stones. After 24 hours, fill the gaps with mortar using a pointing trowel. Clean excess mortar with a wire brush before it hardens.

In hot African climates, stucco can dry too fast and crack. Cover the oven with a wet burlap sack or plastic sheet for the first 3 days. Work in the early morning or late afternoon to avoid direct sun. If cracks appear, fill them with a thin cement slurry. Always wear gloves and a dust mask when mixing cement. A well-applied stucco finish will last 10+ years if you maintain it.

lessons.title: Building a Decorative Arch or Facade
lessons.body:
A decorative arch or facade turns a plain oven into a beautiful feature. For a 12-pizza oven, the opening is usually 45 cm wide and 30 cm high. You will build the arch over this opening using firebricks or cut stones. First, make a wooden template (centering) from plywood that matches the curve of your arch. Support it with wooden posts inside the oven opening. The template holds the bricks in place until the mortar sets.

Mix fire clay mortar: 1 part fire clay, 1 part Portland cement, 3 parts sharp sand, and water to a stiff paste. Lay the arch bricks on the template, starting from both sides and meeting at the top. Use a rubber mallet to tap them into place. The arch must be at least 20 cm deep (two bricks thick) to support the weight above. After laying, let the mortar cure for 48 hours before removing the template.

For a facade, you can build a decorative wall around the oven mouth using bricks or stones. A simple design is a rectangular facade with a curved top that mimics the arch. Leave a 5 cm gap between the facade and the oven dome for expansion. Fill this gap with ceramic fibre insulation or sand. You can also add a chimney arch if your oven has a chimney.

In Africa, many builders use local materials like laterite stone or granite. Clean the stones and wet them before laying. Use a string line to keep the facade straight and level. After the mortar dries, you can paint the facade with a cement paint or leave it natural. A well-built arch will last for decades and become the centrepiece of your outdoor kitchen.

lessons.title: Weatherproofing the Oven
lessons.body:
Weatherproofing protects your oven from rain, sun, and temperature changes. In Africa, intense sun and heavy rains can crack the dome and ruin insulation. The first step is to ensure the oven has a roof or a waterproof render. A simple roof can be made from corrugated iron sheets or thatch supported by wooden posts. The roof should extend at least 30 cm beyond the oven on all sides.

If you cannot build a roof, apply a waterproof render. Mix 1 part cement, 2 parts sand, and a waterproofing additive (like Sika or similar) following the manufacturer's instructions. Apply two coats, each 5 mm thick, over the stucco. Let the first coat dry for 24 hours before the second. The final coat should slope away from the chimney so water runs off. You can also use a breathable waterproof paint designed for masonry.

Check for cracks around the chimney and door. Seal any gaps with high-temperature silicone sealant. For the dome, you can apply a layer of bitumen membrane, but only if the oven is already insulated and the membrane is not in contact with the hot surface. Never use plastic sheeting as it traps moisture and causes rot.

In areas with termites, treat wooden supports with anti-termite solution. Raise the oven base at least 15 cm above ground to prevent water pooling. After a heavy rain, inspect the oven for water stains or soft spots. Repair any damage immediately. A well-weatherproofed oven can be used year-round, even in the rainy season.

lessons.title: Installing a Door and Door Frame
lessons.body:
A door keeps heat in and rain out. For a 12-pizza oven, the door opening is typically 45 cm wide and 30 cm high. You will need a metal door frame and a door made of cast iron, steel, or wood with a metal heat shield. The frame must be embedded into the oven mouth. Use firebricks to build the frame sides, leaving a 2 cm gap for expansion. Fill the gap with ceramic fibre rope.

Make the door from 5 mm steel plate. Weld a handle on the outside and a heat shield on the inside. The door should fit snugly but not too tight. Add a latch to keep it closed. For a wood door, line the inside with aluminium flashing and attach a wooden handle with long bolts. Never use galvanised metal because it releases toxic fumes when heated.

Install the door frame with high-temperature mortar. Let it cure for 24 hours. Then attach the door with hinges. Test the door by closing it and checking for gaps. If you see light through the edges, adjust the frame or add a gasket made from fibreglass rope. The door should open fully without hitting the arch.

In Africa, many ovens use a simple metal door that slides into grooves. This is cheap and effective. You can also use a cast-iron pot lid as a door if it fits. Always keep the door slightly open during firing to allow air flow. After cooking, close the door to retain heat. A good door can keep the oven hot for 4-6 hours.

lessons.title: Adding a Tile or Brick Landing
lessons.body:
A landing is the flat surface in front of the oven where you place pizzas, tools, and fuel. For a 12-pizza oven, make the landing at least 60 cm deep and 90 cm wide. Use bricks, tiles, or stone. The landing should be at the same height as the oven floor so you can slide pizzas in easily. If the oven floor is 1 metre high, build the landing at 1 metre.

Start by laying a concrete base 5 cm thick. Let it cure for 48 hours. Then lay tiles or bricks with a mortar mix of 1 part cement to 3 parts sand. For tiles, use a notched trowel to spread thin-set mortar. Press each tile firmly and check with a spirit level. Leave 3 mm gaps between tiles for grout. For bricks, lay them in a herringbone pattern for strength. Tap them level with a rubber mallet.

After 24 hours, grout the tiles with a cement-based grout. Mix grout with water to a paste, then push it into the gaps with a rubber float. Wipe off excess with a damp sponge. Let it cure for 24 hours before using. If using natural stone, seal it with a stone sealer to prevent stains.

The landing must slope slightly away from the oven (1-2 degrees) so water runs off. In Africa, you can use local materials like terracotta tiles or granite slabs. Avoid smooth glazed tiles because they become slippery when wet. A brick landing is cheap and provides good grip. After building, keep the landing clean and free of ash. A well-built landing makes your oven safer and more efficient.

lessons.title: Final Curing and Cosmetic Touches
lessons.body:
Final curing removes moisture from the oven and prevents cracks. After all exterior work is done, wait at least 7 days before curing. Then build a small fire using dry twigs and paper. Keep it small for 2 hours. The next day, build a slightly larger fire for 3 hours. Repeat this for 5 days, increasing the fire size each day. On the final day, the oven should be hot enough to bake pizza. This slow curing drives out water without steam pressure.

During curing, watch for steam escaping from the dome. If you see cracks, stop and let the oven cool. Fill cracks with a thin slurry of fire clay and water. After curing, the oven may have a white powder on the surface (efflorescence). Brush it off with a stiff brush. You can also apply a coat of linseed oil or masonry sealer to the exterior for a shiny finish.

Cosmetic touches include painting the facade, adding a chimney cap, and installing a thermometer. Use heat-resistant paint for the oven door. For the facade, use cement paint or acrylic. Add a small roof over the chimney to keep rain out. A thermometer (0-500Â°C) mounted on the door helps you monitor temperature. You can also add a metal ash drawer under the oven.

In Africa, many builders decorate with mosaic tiles or carved wood. Keep decorations away from hot surfaces. After curing, test the oven by baking a pizza. If the crust cooks in 90 seconds, the oven is ready. Maintain the oven by cleaning ash weekly and checking for cracks monthly. A well-cured oven will serve you for many years.

lessons.title: Practical Reference
lessons.body:
Practical Reference: Finishing the Oven Exterior

Finishing a wood-fired pizza oven is where craft becomes commerce. In the African context â from Nairobi's artisan pizza scene to Cape Town's weekend market traders and Lagos's growing food-truck economy â the exterior finish determines whether your oven survives the rainy season, whether customers trust your brand, and whether you can charge premium prices. This module covers the practical sequence: stucco or stone veneer, decorative arch/facade, weatherproofing, door installation, tile or brick landing, and final curing. Every step is framed around durability, cost control, and customer perception.

1. Applying Stucco or Stone Veneer

Stucco is the workhorse finish across Africa: cheap, repairable, and effective when mixed correctly. The classic mix is 1 part cement : 3 parts sharp sand : 1 part lime, applied in two coats over chicken wire fixed to the insulation blanket. In humid coastal markets (Mombasa, Durban, Lagos), add a waterproofing admixture or use a 1:2:1 mix with acrylic bonding agent. Stone veneer â local granite, sandstone, or river stone â costs 3â5Ã more but signals premium quality; a Nairobi restaurant using river-stone veneer can charge 20â30% more per pizza than a plain-stucco competitor.

Table 1: Exterior finish options â cost and performance comparison (2024 prices, East & Southern Africa)
FinishCost (USD/mÂ²)Durability (years)Best for
Cement stucco (2-coat)8â158â12Budget commercial ovens, high-volume markets
Stucco + waterproof admixture12â2012â18Coastal/humid regions
Local stone veneer35â6020â30Premium restaurants, tourism lodges
Clay/earth render (traditional)4â95â8Rural, low-cost builds; needs annual maintenance
Ceramic tile cladding25â4515â25Urban food courts, easy-clean surfaces

Source: Compiled from FAO Wood-Fired Oven Construction Guide (2019), Kenya Association of Manufacturers building materials price survey (2024), and SANS 10400 masonry cost data.

2. Building a Decorative Arch or Facade

The arch is your brand. It frames the oven mouth, protects the door, and creates the visual signature customers photograph. Build a semicircular arch from firebrick or cut stone using a wooden formwork that stays in place until the mortar cures (minimum 48 hours in hot climates, 72 hours in humid conditions). The arch should span 10â15 cm wider than the oven mouth on each side. For facades, use a simple brick or stone surround that hides the insulation and chimney transition. In Lagos and Accra, decorative concrete lintels with painted motifs are popular and cost-effective.

3. Weatherproofing the Oven

Water is the number-one killer of wood-fired ovens in Africa. A single rainy season can crack a poorly sealed dome. Weatherproofing has three layers: (1) a waterproof render coat with acrylic or silicone admixture; (2) a chimney cowl to stop rain entering the flue; (3) a raised base or damp-proof course to stop ground moisture wicking up. In high-rainfall zones (Kampala, Douala, Kigali), add a small roof or canopy over the oven â a 2 mÂ² corrugated iron roof costs under USD 60 and can double oven lifespan.

â  SAFETY WARNING â Carbon Monoxide & Structural Risk

Never cure, fire, or operate an oven indoors or in a fully enclosed space without a certified flue and CO alarm. Carbon monoxide from wood combustion is odourless and lethal â at least 4 deaths per year in East Africa are linked to poorly vented ovens and braziers (WHO, 2023). Ensure the chimney extends at least 1 m above the roofline and 3 m from any window. Never seal the oven exterior before the dome has fully cured â trapped moisture causes explosive spalling. Wear N95 masks when mixing cement and cutting firebrick; silica dust causes silicosis.

4. Installing a Door and Door Frame

The door controls heat retention and is the single biggest factor in fuel efficiency. A well-fitted cast-iron or steel door with a fibre-glass rope gasket retains heat for 6â8 hours after firing, letting you bake bread the next morning â a major revenue stream. The frame must be set into the arch with fire-rated mortar and must not touch the oven mouth directly (leave a 3â5 mm expansion gap). In Africa, local metal fabricators can produce custom doors for USD 40â90, versus USD 200+ for imported units.

Table 2: Door types â heat retention, cost, and business impact
Door typeHeat retentionCost (USD)Best use
Cast iron + gasket6â8 hrs80â150Restaurants baking bread + pizza
Steel plate + gasket5â7 hrs40â90Market traders, food trucks
Stainless steel insulated7â10 hrs150â300Premium bakeries, hotels
No door (open mouth)1â2 hrs0High-volume pizza-only operations

Source: Adapted from the Practical Action Wood-Fired Oven Technical Brief (2021) and the Kenya Industrial Research and Development Institute (KIRDI) Small-Scale Bakery Equipment Guide (2022).

5. Adding a Tile or Brick Landing

The landing is where the pizza meets the customer â it must be level, heat-resistant, and easy to clean. Use terracotta tiles, quarry tiles, or firebrick laid in a sand-cement bed with a slight 2% slope away from the oven mouth for drainage. A 60 Ã 40 cm landing is the practical minimum for a 12" pizza operation. In dusty environments, seal the landing with a food-safe tile sealer to prevent dust ingress. This is also the ideal spot for your prep station: flour bin, topping trays, and a peel hook.

6. Final Curing and Cosmetic Touches

Curing is non-negotiable. After finishing, wait 7 days (28 days in humid climates) before the first fire. Then fire gradually: small fire day 1, medium day 2, full fire day 3. This drives out residual moisture and prevents cracking. Cosmetic touches â a painted facade, a chalkboard menu, LED strip lighting under the arch, a branded door handle â cost little but raise perceived value. A well-finished oven photographed for social media is free marketing; many African pizza businesses report 30â40% of first-time customers arrive via Instagram or TikTok after seeing the oven.

Quick Reference Checklist

  • â Mix stucco 1:3:1 (cement:sand:lime) and apply in two coats over chicken wire.
  • â Keep arch formwork in place 48â72 hours before removing.
  • â Apply waterproof render + fit chimney cowl before rainy season.
  • â Leave 3â5 mm expansion gap between door frame and oven mouth.
  • â Slope landing 2% away from oven for drainage.
  • â Cure 7 days minimum, then fire gradually over 3 days.
  • â Fit CO alarm and ensure chimney clears roofline by 1 m.
  • â Seal landing with food-safe sealer; add branded cosmetic touches.

Further Reading

  • FAO â Wood-Fired Oven Construction Guide (PDF, free)
  • Practical Action â Technical Briefs on Oven & Stove Construction
  • WHO â Household Air Pollution & Health Guidelines
  • South African Bureau of Standards (SANS 10400 â Building Code)
  • KIRDI â Kenya Industrial Research & Development Institute Equipment Guides

Business takeaway: A properly finished oven is not a cost centre â it is a revenue asset. Stucco and stone veneer protect your capital, the arch markets your brand, the door extends your product line into bread and pastries, and the landing speeds up service. Budget 15â25% of your total oven cost for finishing, and you will get an oven that lasts 15+ years and pays for itself within one season.

quiz.q: What is the correct cement-to-sand ratio for the scratch coat of stucco?
quiz.explanation: The scratch coat uses a richer mix of 1 part cement to 3 parts sand for strength.

quiz.q: How thick should the scratch coat of stucco be applied?
quiz.explanation: The scratch coat is applied about 1 cm thick to provide a base for subsequent coats.

quiz.q: What tool is used to create grooves in the scratch coat?
quiz.explanation: A nail or rake scratches the surface to create grooves for the next coat to grip.

quiz.q: How long should you wait before removing the wooden template from a decorative arch?
quiz.explanation: The mortar needs 48 hours to cure enough to support the arch bricks without the template.

quiz.q: What is the minimum depth for an arch in a 12-pizza oven?
quiz.explanation: The arch should be at least 20 cm deep (two bricks thick) to support the weight above.

quiz.q: What material is used to fill the gap between the facade and the oven dome?
quiz.explanation: Ceramic fibre insulation fills the expansion gap and insulates the oven.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid using plastic sheeting to weatherproof an oven?
options: B) It traps moisture and causes rot
C) It melts in the sun
D) It is not available in Africa
quiz.explanation: Plastic sheeting traps moisture inside the oven, leading to rot and damage.

quiz.q: What is the recommended thickness for a waterproof render coat?
quiz.explanation: Each waterproof render coat should be about 5 mm thick for effective protection.

quiz.q: What type of sealant should be used around the chimney and door?
quiz.explanation: High-temperature silicone sealant withstands the heat without degrading.

quiz.q: How high should the oven base be raised above ground to prevent water pooling?
quiz.explanation: Raising the base at least 15 cm prevents water from pooling around the oven.

quiz.q: What is the typical door opening size for a 12-pizza oven?
options: A) 30 cm wide x 20 cm high
B) 45 cm wide x 30 cm high
C) 60 cm wide x 40 cm high
D) 50 cm wide x 25 cm high
quiz.explanation: A 12-pizza oven typically has a door opening of 45 cm wide and 30 cm high.

quiz.q: What material should never be used for an oven door due to toxic fumes?
quiz.explanation: Galvanised metal releases toxic fumes when heated and should never be used.

quiz.q: What is used to fill the gap between the door frame and the oven mouth?
quiz.explanation: Ceramic fibre rope fills the expansion gap and provides a heat seal.

quiz.q: How long should you wait before attaching the door after installing the frame?
quiz.explanation: The high-temperature mortar needs 24 hours to cure before attaching the door.

quiz.q: What is the recommended depth for a landing in front of a 12-pizza oven?
quiz.explanation: A landing at least 60 cm deep provides enough space for pizzas and tools.

quiz.q: What is the correct mortar mix for laying tiles or bricks on a landing?
quiz.explanation: A mix of 1 part cement to 3 parts sand is standard for laying tiles and bricks.

quiz.q: How much should the landing slope away from the oven?
quiz.explanation: A slight slope of 1-2 degrees allows water to run off without affecting stability.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid smooth glazed tiles for the landing?
options: C) They become slippery when wet
D) They are not available in Africa
quiz.explanation: Smooth glazed tiles become dangerously slippery when wet, especially in outdoor kitchens.

quiz.q: How long should you wait after finishing exterior work before starting the curing fires?
quiz.explanation: Wait at least 7 days to allow the exterior finishes to set before curing the oven.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of curing the oven with small fires?
options: B) To drive out moisture slowly
quiz.explanation: Slow curing drives out moisture without creating steam pressure that can crack the oven.

quiz.q: What should you do if you see steam escaping from the dome during curing?
options: B) Stop and let the oven cool
quiz.explanation: Steam indicates moisture is still escaping; stop and cool to prevent cracks.

quiz.q: What is efflorescence on the oven surface?
options: B) A white powder from salts
quiz.explanation: Efflorescence is a white powder of salts that can be brushed off after curing.

quiz.q: What can be applied to the exterior for a shiny finish after curing?
options: B) Linseed oil or masonry sealer
quiz.explanation: Linseed oil or masonry sealer provides a protective, shiny finish.

quiz.q: What is the ideal cooking time for a pizza in a properly cured oven?
quiz.explanation: A wood-fired oven at proper temperature cooks a pizza in about 90 seconds.

quiz.q: How often should you clean ash from the oven?
quiz.explanation: Weekly cleaning of ash keeps the oven efficient and prevents buildup.

quiz.q: What is the best time of day to apply stucco in hot African climates?
options: B) Early morning or late afternoon
quiz.explanation: Working in early morning or late afternoon avoids rapid drying and cracking from direct sun.

quiz.q: What is the recommended gap between stones when applying stone veneer?
quiz.explanation: A 1 cm gap between stones allows for proper mortar filling and expansion.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a chimney cap?
quiz.explanation: A chimney cap prevents rain from entering the chimney and damaging the oven.

quiz.q: What type of thermometer is recommended for a wood-fired oven?
quiz.explanation: A 0-500Â°C thermometer covers the full range of wood-fired oven temperatures.

quiz.q: What is the best way to maintain the oven after curing?
options: B) Clean ash weekly and check for cracks monthly
quiz.explanation: Regular cleaning and monthly inspections keep the oven in good condition.
